title: J4 — Crossing back
description: The family shares his full record with a Thai doctor using a link on Dad’s phone.

steps.title: One phone holds the whole family’s records
steps.headline: A year on, the family plans a trip to Thailand. Bounmy’s phone holds records for all three of them, including Somsack’s six verified doses.
steps.touchpoint: Family wallet app on Dad’s phone
steps.narrative:
The family plans a trip to Thailand. Bounmy's phone holds the
family wallet, with a profile for each of them. Somsack's summary
(`TrustDemoJ4Ips`) shows six doses: two from Thailand, four from Lao PDR.

experiences.doing: Opens the family wallet: profiles for himself, Khamla and Somsack.
experiences.feeling: “One phone, three people — I can manage all of us.”

experiences.doing: Relies on Bounmy’s phone for her own and the baby’s records.
experiences.feeling: “It’s on his phone. What if I travel without him?”

steps.painPoint: Many families share one smartphone; one-app-per-person designs leave them out.
steps.enabler: A household wallet on one phone, with a separate health summary for each person.

handoff.summary: Somsack’s summary is ready to share

whatIf.outcome: Who can access the baby’s record without Bounmy’s phone? Delegated access within a household is still an open design question.

steps.title: Dad creates a link to share at the clinic
steps.headline: Before the trip, Bounmy creates a QR link for Somsack’s record, locked with a 4-digit passcode and valid for 14 days (the demo’s settings: each country would set its own). The record itself stays in Lao PDR.

preconditions.title: Country B's DSC is shared with the trust anchor
preconditions.description: **Precondition, as in J1:** Country B's DSC, under Country B's CSCA, is already shared with the GDHCN, the Trust Anchor. That is what lets the clinic in Thailand verify the link in J4.1.

steps.narrative:
For Somsack, Bounmy shares his record with a 4-digit passcode he
can say aloud, valid for 14 days. The portal records his consent
(`TrustDemoJ4Consent`), then does three things:

1. It assembles the IPS and Somsack's DVCs.
2. It encrypts them (STT-VHL-004, STT-VHL-007) behind a passcode-protected manifest with an expiry (STT-VHL-009).
3. It issues the link as an HCERT, with the VHL at key 5 (STT-VHL-001, STT-VHL-002), signed with Country B's DSC.

The QR holds only a pointer and a key: the record stays in Lao PDR.

experiences.doing: Creates a passcode-protected QR link for Somsack, valid for 14 days.
experiences.feeling: “I decide who sees it, and for how long.”

steps.painPoint: Sending photos or PDFs of records leaks data and can’t be verified by the receiver.
steps.enabler: A Verifiable Health Link: the QR holds only a locked pointer; the data stays home until the passcode is given.

record.description: Shareable link created; data stays in Lao PDR
record.heldWhere: Lao national records (QR is just a pointer)

handoff.summary: A QR on Dad’s phone + a passcode he can say aloud

whatIf.scenario: Bounmy’s phone battery dies at the clinic.
whatIf.outcome: The link could be printed in advance, and the original paper cards still prove the birth doses.

steps.title: A Thai doctor sees the full history
steps.headline: Back where it all began, Dr. Anan scans the link, hears the passcode, and sees Somsack’s whole first year — and Lao PDR is told who looked.

preconditions.title: The DID documents are already loaded
preconditions.description: **Precondition, as in J3: the DID documents are already loaded.** The clinic viewer's trust store is a cached copy of the GDHCN trust list, including Country B's DSC DID document (STT-TRU-001, STT-TRU-002, STT-TRU-005). The clinic refreshes it nightly or hourly, against about weekly at the offline J3 clinic. It does not need to be online to verify: verifying reads the cache and never fetches the list. A DSC published after the last refresh fails the trust-list check (STT-VER-006), naming that reason.

steps.narrative:
Back where it began, Dr Anan sees Somsack at a primary care clinic in
Chiang Rai. Bounmy shows the QR on his phone and says the passcode. The
clinic viewer and the Lao gateway take five steps:

1. The viewer verifies the HCERT against Country B's DSC in its copy of the trust list.
2. It requests the manifest by ITI-YY5, signed with HTTP Message Signatures (STT-VHL-005, STT-VHL-006, STT-VHL-008).
3. The Lao gateway checks the passcode, the expiry and the consent, returns the manifest, and logs the access at home (`TrustDemoJ41Access`).
4. The viewer decrypts the IPS and DVCs (STT-VHL-007) (`TrustDemoJ41Received`).
5. It shows them to Dr Anan: every dose since the birth, viewed, never copied.

A wrong passcode is refused, and the attempt is still logged in Lao PDR
(`TrustDemoJ41WrongPasscode`). If the HCERT does not verify (for example,
Country B's DSC is missing from the cached list), there is no digital
verification. The clinic names the step and the reason (STT-VER-008), does not
follow the VHL, and Dr Anan treats whatever the family can show as he
would a paper record.

experiences.doing: Scans the QR, enters the passcode Bounmy tells him, and sees all six doses.
experiences.feeling: “Born here, vaccinated there — and I can see all of it.”

experiences.doing: Back in Chiang Rai with a fever, he is seen by the doctor who vaccinated him at birth.
experiences.feeling: “A strange room, but nobody has to guess what he has had.”

experiences.doing: Shows the QR on his phone and says the passcode out loud.
Watches the doctor see everything that happened since the birth.

steps.painPoint: Without the history, the doctor would repeat vaccines or have to guess.
steps.enabler: The record is fetched live from Lao PDR, viewed without being copied, and an access log is sent home.

record.description: Viewed in Thailand, never copied; access logged in Lao PDR

handoff.summary: Journey complete — full circle back to Thailand

whatIf.outcome: Access is refused and the attempt is still logged back in Lao PDR.
